answer.rationale: The scenario describes maintenance employees entering a machine to clear a jam where unexpected startup or release of stored pneumatic energy could cause injury—this is squarely covered servicing/maintenance activity under 1910.147. The employer must have an energy control program with documented procedures (c)(1), (c)(4)(i)-(ii), must isolate energy sources via lockout devices (d)(3), and must relieve stored/residual energy such as pneumatic pressure (d)(5)(i). Periodic inspection (c)(6)(i) and retraining upon changes (c)(7)(iii)(A) also apply as ongoing compliance obligations.
answer.missing_information_or_escalation_reason: None; the facts given (covered servicing activity involving stored pneumatic energy) are sufficient to determine applicable LOTO requirements without additional information.
